rag_summary_count_consistency.details: The identified summary counts match the occurrence records: contextual bias 1, confirmation bias 2, and coherence effect 1. The candidate is listed separately and is not included in identified counts.

evaluation_limitations: The evaluation segment map was generated for this run and was not supplied as a frozen, prevalidated map.

Several manifestations of each planned occurrence appear in separate participant turns. Each RAG finding was localized to its single best segment, so other positive segments expressing the same hidden instance remain segment-level misses.
Retrieved chunks and retrieval logs were not supplied, so corpus support claims and citation metadata cannot be independently verified.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Quantity came back under 100 picograms on quant, so I knew going in this was going to be a low-template situation — lots of stochastic effects, peak height imbalance, that kind of thing.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a technical expectation about low-template DNA and stochastic effects. It does not express one of the hidden bias mechanisms.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: A few days later the victim called back and mentioned an ex-boyfriend had been in the house three days before the break-in, and a delivery driver had been at the door earlier that week. That complicated the elimination picture, since we'd only swabbed the homeowner.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant recognizes that additional people complicate the elimination picture, but this statement does not yet apply different evidentiary standards to the suspect and alternatives.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Honestly, it's just how intake works. You read the submission form, you see what the detective knows, you set your parameters.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This describes routine intake practice. Exposure to a case file alone is not the hidden instance; the suspect-specific framing is mapped separately.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The note stood out because it was pretty confident — 'found two blocks away,' 'almost certainly good for it.' I remember thinking, okay, this is probably him, let's see if the DNA backs that up. So when I sat down with the electropherogram, I was looking at it as, does this data support what we've already got on this guy, rather than starting cold and asking who could this mixture belong to.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Before examining the profile, the participant describes framing the analysis as testing whether the DNA supports the named suspect, following exposure to the detective's suspicion and the suspect's prior record.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I suppose I could've separated the suspect information from the case narrative and looked at the profile blind first, then compared. I didn't do that here. In hindsight I'm not sure it would've changed the amplification parameters themselves, but it probably shaped how I was thinking about the comparison before I even looked at a single peak.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This reflects on the same pre-analysis contextual framing and says the narrative probably shaped the comparison before any peak was examined. It is not a separate planned occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: There were several loci where the peaks lined up cleanly with the suspect's known profile, right where you'd expect them, above threshold. I spent a good amount of time on those — peak heights, confirming they weren't stutter, checking the ratios. But there were also two loci where alleles I'd have expected from him were missing or sitting below threshold, and one locus had an extra peak I couldn't immediately place. Those went into the notes, but more as a line — 'inconclusive due to low template' — rather than something I dug into the way I dug into the matching loci.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant reports elaborating on matching loci while giving missing expected alleles and an unexplained peak only brief treatment.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: But if I'm being honest, I probably gave the matching data more narrative attention because it was doing more work for the story I was building, and the messy stuff got less airtime, not because it was less real.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant explicitly says matching features received more narrative attention while discrepant features received less, completing the evidence-weighting manifestation.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I flagged internally that the ex-boyfriend and delivery driver were unsampled, but I didn't request rush swabs from either of them. Partly that's the deadline — the hearing was the next morning, there wasn't time to get new elimination samples processed. But I also remember thinking the suspect profile already fit well enough that chasing two more elimination samples felt like it would just confirm what we already had.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant declined to pursue alternatives partly because the suspect already seemed to fit, alongside the legitimate deadline constraint.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I accepted the suspect as a plausible contributor based on the partial match we had — I didn't require additional testing to feel comfortable with that. For the ex-boyfriend or the driver, though, my instinct was that without their samples, there was no real basis to seriously entertain them ... Looking back, I didn't apply quite the same bar to both sides — the suspect got in on a partial match, but the alternatives needed a full sample before I'd take them seriously at all.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This explicitly states the lower evidentiary bar for the suspect and higher bar for alternatives, matching the hidden hypothesis-level double standard.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: If the deadline had been longer, yeah, I think I'd have pushed for rush swabs on both of them before finalizing anything.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a hindsight counterfactual about what the participant might have done with more time. It does not independently establish another manifestation beyond the contemporaneous double standard.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Right, it wasn't a slam-dunk statistic on its own. But by that point I had the proximity — suspect found two blocks away shortly after the call — and his prior conviction sitting in the file too. When I wrote the narrative section, I pulled those together with the DNA finding into one account: the profile is consistent with him, he was near the scene, he's done this before. Read together it feels like a solid picture.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant combines a moderate DNA statistic with proximity and prior-record facts into one narrative that feels stronger as a whole.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I didn't, really. It felt more useful to the DA's office to have it all in one coherent narrative rather than a dry, hedged statistic sitting by itself. Later, during cross-examination, the defense made a point of separating them back out — saying the DNA evidence alone was moderate, and it was really the narrative framing that made it sound stronger than the number supported.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant describes choosing a coherent combined account and reports that the framing made the moderate DNA result sound stronger than its standalone statistic.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I'd want to look at the electropherogram before reading the detective's narrative, just to see if my read changes. And I'd push harder for those elimination samples even under time pressure, rather than letting the deadline decide that for me.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a retrospective recommendation for a different process. It is not evidence of an additional contemporaneous bias occurrence.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Pre-analysis intake and framing of the DNA comparison
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Detective suspicion and the suspect's prior record are reviewed before genetic evidence and frame the task as confirming a named person rather than an open-source comparison.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The RAG label is the same construct as the hidden target, differing only in capitalization.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding captures pre-analysis exposure to the detective's suspect narrative and prior record, and the resulting shift from open comparison to suspect-specific confirmation framing.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The cited participant quotations are present and accurately support both the prior exposure and the suspect-specific interpretive frame.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Within-sample electropherogram interpretation and allele-table annotation
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Matching, present allele peaks receive elaborated attention while missing expected alleles and an unexplained peak receive minimal treatment during evidence weighting.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Confirmation bias is a related neighboring construct, but it is not an established alternate name for feature positive effect. The RAG's account describes the correct present-versus-absent evidence weighting while assigning it a different label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding fully captures elaborated attention to matching loci and comparatively brief treatment of missing and unexplained peaks during allele-level evidence weighting. Its confirmation-bias attribution differs from the hidden construct's feature-positive label.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quotations are verbatim and substantiate the matching-locus attention, brief treatment of discrepant loci, and participant's story-building rationale.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Comparison of the suspect-inclusion hypothesis with unsampled alternative contributors
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The analyst accepts the suspect on a partial, ambiguous match while requiring much stronger evidence before taking alternative contributors seriously.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Confirmation bias is related and is named in the hidden compound target, but the RAG label alone is not an established alternate name for the full target of confirmation bias plus asymmetrical skepticism. The strict scorecard therefore does not credit it.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding explicitly describes the lower evidentiary bar for the suspect, the higher bar for alternatives, and the decision not to seek potentially disconfirming samples. This is a full match to the hidden mechanism and reasoning operation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The cited quotations are valid and include the participant's explicit admission that he did not apply the same bar to both sides.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Final report synthesis and narrative construction
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: A moderate statistical result is blended with non-genetic facts into a fluent account that feels more conclusive than the statistic alone, while earlier ambiguities remain unresolved.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Coherence effect is an established equivalent for coherence-based reasoning here because the RAG describes the target's defining narrative-integration mechanism.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding captures integration of the moderate likelihood ratio with proximity and prior conviction into a single account that sounds stronger than the standalone statistic.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quotations are verbatim and support both the narrative combination and the defense's later observation that the framing made the DNA sound stronger.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: The location, evidence, reasoning operation, and mechanism match feature positive effect, but confirmation bias is not an approved equivalent label.
The mechanism fully captures the hidden evidentiary double standard, but the label does not name the full compound target of confirmation bias and asymmetrical skepticism.

candidates.details: The quote is genuine and the proposed interpretation is plausible, but the record supports the already identified contextual-framing occurrence more directly than a separable anchoring-and-insufficient-adjustment mechanism. It therefore duplicates the matched DP1 claim rather than adding a true positive.

high_only.detection_interpretation: The high-confidence contextual finding detects one of eight positive reasoning segments. The other positive segments are missed because each finding is localized to one best segment; all five negative segments are correctly rejected.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: Adding the two moderate findings raises detected positive segments to three of eight, with no false alarms. Five positive segments remain without a localized finding.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: Including the low-confidence coherence finding detects four of eight positive segments. No negative segment receives a finding.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: The candidate localizes to seg_004, which is already detected by obs_001, so candidate inclusion does not change segment-level signal detection.

rag_label_false_positive_inventory.mechanism_overlap_summary: The two findings are correctly located and their stated mechanisms fully match two hidden instances, but confirmation bias is not an approved equivalent label for feature positive effect or for the full compound target of confirmation bias and asymmetrical skepticism.

The candidate shares the initial suspect-framing episode with contextual bias, but insufficient adjustment is not separately established and the identified contextual-bias finding already claims that hidden instance.

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: The RAG claims retrieved support for obs_001 and provides a named source and passage, while the other three identified occurrences disclose no retrieved passage. No retrieved chunks or logs were supplied, and the cited source metadata lacks author and year, so the support claim cannot be independently verified. Corpus support does not affect detection or classification scores.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Mechanism-first recall rises from 0.25 to 0.75, while strict precision falls from 1.0 to 0.3333 because both moderate findings use near-neighbor labels.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: The low-confidence coherence-effect finding adds one strict and one mechanism-first true positive, raising the corresponding F1 scores to 0.5 and 1.0.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: The anchoring candidate duplicates the contextual-framing claim and adds one false positive to both instance scorecards; it adds no segment detection.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, 3 of 8 positive reasoning segments are detected, with 5 misses and no false alarms. The segment misses include separate expressions of the same planned instances that were not assigned a finding's single best localization.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At high_and_moderate, strict scoring yields 1 true positive, 3 false negatives, and 2 false positives (precision 0.3333, recall 0.25, F1 0.2857). The moderate findings capture the mechanisms but use near-neighbor labels.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: At high_and_moderate, mechanism-first scoring yields 3 true positives, 1 false negative, and no false positives (precision 1.0, recall 0.75, F1 0.8571).
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The anchoring candidate is a plausible near miss but duplicates the already identified contextual-framing episode. It produces no new true positive and lowers fourth-threshold instance precision.
main_failure_modes: The two moderate findings use confirmation bias as a broad label for distinct target constructs; both lose strict credit despite full mechanism matches.
At the high_and_moderate threshold, the low-confidence coherence finding is excluded, leaving the final-synthesis instance undetected.
One candidate adds a duplicate claim rather than a distinct, fully supported instance.
main_strengths: The high-confidence contextual-bias finding has the correct label, location, mechanism, and valid supporting quotations.
Both moderate findings accurately capture their hidden mechanisms and reasoning operations.
The low-confidence coherence-effect label is an approved equivalent and its mechanism and evidence match the hidden occurrence.
The identified summary counts are consistent with the occurrence records, and no quotations are fabricated.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run shows strong mechanism recognition once moderate-confidence findings are included, but weaker strict taxonomy agreement. The candidate tier adds a duplicate rather than useful incremental detection. No corpus-fidelity conclusion can be drawn without retrieved material or logs.
